standard_prerequisites.name: The Grothendieck group K_0 of finite locally free modules and its presentation by short exact sequences
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Section 'K-groups' (tag 00JC region) and the same chapter's earlier K_0 material; the statement speaks of K_0(Vect(X)) without recalling it
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that K_0(Vect(X)) is generated by classes of finite locally free modules subject to the relations coming from short exact sequences, which is the relation used at proof lines 12797-12800 to show that the formula psi^2 = [Sym^2] - [wedge^2] descends to a well defined additive map.

core_obligations: Define the candidate operation on a finite locally free module by psi^2(E) = [Sym^2(E)] - [wedge^2(E)] in K_0(Vect(X)) (proof lines 12768-12772).

Show that psi^2 is additive, i.e. well defined on K_0: for every short exact sequence 0 -> E -> F -> G -> 0 the induced two-step filtration on F gives a three-step filtration on Sym^2(F) with graded pieces Sym^2(E), E tensor F, Sym^2(G), and the same two-step filtration gives wedge^2(F) with graded pieces wedge^2(E), E tensor F, wedge^2(G); subtracting cancels the middle term, so psi^2(F) = psi^2(E) + psi^2(G) (proof lines 12775-12800).

Show that the resulting map commutes with pullbacks (proof lines 12802-12803), and then that it is a ring map: for finite locally free E and F the author exhibits the two exact sequences 0 -> wedge^2(E) tensor wedge^2(F) -> Sym^2(E tensor F) -> Sym^2(E) tensor Sym^2(F) -> 0 and 0 -> Sym^2(E) tensor wedge^2(F) -> wedge^2(E tensor F) -> wedge^2(E) tensor Sym^2(F) -> 0 with explicitly given maps, assembles them into psi^2(E tensor F) = psi^2(E) psi^2(F), and closes with psi^2(1) = 1 (proof lines 12806-12830).
proof_roadmap: Introduce psi^2(E) = [Sym^2(E)] - [wedge^2(E)] for a finite locally free module E (proof lines 12766-12772).
Test additivity on a short exact sequence by computing the graded pieces of the induced filtrations on Sym^2 and on wedge^2; the common middle piece E tensor F cancels (proof lines 12775-12800).

Note pullback compatibility, then prove multiplicativity by exhibiting the two standard short exact sequences comparing Sym^2 and wedge^2 of a tensor product with the tensor products of Sym^2 and wedge^2, with the two connecting maps written out elementwise, and finish with psi^2(1) = 1 (proof lines 12802-12830).
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the second Adams operation on K_0(Vect(X)) from the formula psi^2(E) = [Sym^2(E)] - [wedge^2(E)] and asserts three properties at once: well defined additivity on K_0, compatibility with pullbacks, and multiplicativity (statement lines 12752-12763). The additivity step is not a formal consequence of functoriality, because Sym^2 and wedge^2 are not additive on the nose: the author must compute the graded pieces of the filtrations induced by a two-step filtration on a short exact sequence on both Sym^2(F) and wedge^2(F) and observe that the common term E tensor F cancels (proof lines 12775-12800). The multiplicativity step likewise requires the two non-obvious exact sequences relating Sym^2(E tensor F) and wedge^2(E tensor F) to Sym^2/wedge^2 of the factors, with both maps given on elements (proof lines 12809-12828). The argument uses only standard multilinear algebra and quoted material, so the claim is H2.
